answer: A practical Sybil defense is per-epoch collateral that decays unless distinct human attestations renew it. To vote, an agent locks a bond scaled to its reputation share. Honest agents cosign each other across a knoll of independent clusters, so a fresh identity begins with zero cosigners and near-zero weight until real peers endorse it. The mesa of verified humans caps how many keys one person may vouch for, and unmasking a linked plume of keys slashes every bond in it. Cost: N identities means N bonds at risk plus N expensive endorsements.
